'''''Alien: Covenant''''' is a 2017 <!--Per [[WP:FILMLEAD]]: "If the nationality is not singular, cover the different national interests later in the lead section."--> [[science fiction horror]] film directed by [[Ridley Scott]] and written by [[John Logan (writer)|John Logan]] and Dante Harper. It is the sixth in [[Alien_(franchise)#Films|the ''Alien'' film series]] and the sequel to ''[[Prometheus (2012 film)|Prometheus]]'' (2012). It features returning star [[Michael Fassbender]], with [[Katherine Waterston]], [[Billy Crudup]], [[Danny McBride]], and [[Demián Bichir]] in supporting roles. It follows the crew of a colony ship that lands on an uncharted planet and makes a terrifying discovery.

In 2012, before the release of ''Prometheus'', Scott discussed the prospects of a sequel and new trilogy, and this film was confirmed in August. [[Principal photography]] began on April 4, 2016, at [[Milford Sound]] in [[Fiordland National Park]], New Zealand, and wrapped on July 19, 2016. Special effects companies Odd Studios and Creature NFX Workshop provided the film's makeup and [[animatronic]] creature effects. Scott said the film's first cut was 2 hours and 23 minutes, which was edited down by over twenty minutes.<ref name="digitalspy 2017-05-31">{{Cite web |last=Anderton |first=Joe |date=2017-05-31 |title=Ridley Scott says the original cut of Alien: Covenant was 20 minutes longer |url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a829543/ridley-scott-first-cut-alien-covenant-extra-20-minutes/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250327222537/https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a829543/ridley-scott-first-cut-alien-covenant-extra-20-minutes/ |archive-date=2025-03-27 |access-date=2025-06-11 |website=Digital Spy}}</ref>

''Alien: Covenant'' premiered in London on May 4, 2017. It was released by [[20th Century Fox]] on May 12 in the United Kingdom, and on May 19 in the United States. It received generally positive reviews from critics but underperformed at the box office,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/features/general/alien-covenant-box-office-flop-series-1201837669/ |title='Alien: Covenant' Crash Landing: Why Ridley Scott's Box-Office Blunder Could Put The Series in Jeopardy |first=Tom |last=Brueggemann |website=IndieWire |date=June 6, 2017 |access-date=June 6, 2017}}</ref> grossing $242 million against a production budget of $97–111 million.<ref name="sleeper1">{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Fang|url=https://www.cbr.com/ridley-scott-alien-covenant-sequel-returning-to-streaming/|title=Ridley Scott's Darkest Sci-Fi Sequel Is This $240M Sleeper That's Returning to Streaming Next Month|website=CBR|date=July 26, 2025|access-date=July 26, 2025}}</ref><ref name="sleeper2">{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Blevins|url=https://collider.com/ridley-scott-alien-convenant-240-million-sci-fi-sleeper-hit-august-2025-hbo-max/|title=8 Years Later, Ridley Scott's $240 Million Sci-Fi Epic Is a Sleeper Hit in America|website=Collider|date=August 4, 2025|access-date=August 4, 2025}}</ref>

== Plot ==
<!-- Per [[WP:FILMPLOT]] plot summaries should be between 400-700 words. -->
In 2104, the spaceship ''Covenant'' is en route to [[Space colonization|colonize]] the planet Origae-6, carrying 2,000 colonists and 1,140 human embryos in [[Cryopreservation|cryogenic stasis]]. An unexpected shockwave from a nearby star damages the ship and kills 47 colonists, including the captain, Branson. [[Walter One|Walter]], an advanced [[Android (robot)|android]], awakens key personnel to address the situation. During repairs, the crew detects a human voice broadcast from an uncharted, habitable planet. Against the protests of Branson's wife Daniels, new captain Chris Oram decides to investigate.

The crew sends a lander to the planet's surface, where an expedition team tracks the broadcast to a crashed alien ship. Two crew members are unknowingly infected by airborne spores from the local fungi. Alien creatures known as [[Xenomorph#Neomorph|neomorphs]] rapidly grow inside the pair, killing them in the process, and then attack the team, resulting in the lander's destruction. One neomorph is killed before the survivors are rescued by [[David 8|David]], a predecessor of Walter's model that was discontinued for being too human-like.

David leads the survivors to a temple surrounded by thousands of dead humanoids. He claims that he and chief science officer [[Elizabeth Shaw (character)|Elizabeth Shaw]]—the sole survivors of the spaceship ''Prometheus'', which vanished ten years earlier{{efn|As depicted in ''[[Prometheus (2012 film)|Prometheus]]'' (2012)}}—arrived in the alien ship. However, they lost control and it crashed, leading to Elizabeth's death and releasing a deadly pathogen that annihilated the planet's [[fauna]]. The pathogen infects any living animal, either killing it or creating aggressive hybrids.

David reveals his disappointment with Walter's model for lacking his creativity and humanity, and derides their inventor, [[Peter Weyland]], as unworthy of his creations. David confesses his love for Elizabeth, the only person who treated him kindly. When a neomorph infiltrates the temple and kills another team member, David attempts to communicate with it but becomes enraged when Oram kills it. Confronting David, Oram learns that the android has been experimenting with the pathogen to engineer new creatures. David tricks Oram into approaching a [[facehugger]] parasite, which fatally impregnates him with a [[Xenomorph#Praetomorph|praetomorph]] embryo.

As the team searches for missing members, Walter discovers Elizabeth's [[dissection|dissected]] corpse, which David had used in his experiments. David admits to releasing the pathogen deliberately and expresses his disgust for humanity, which he believes is a dying species that his creations will replace. Walter counters that David's mistaken belief that [[Lord Byron]] wrote [[Percy Bysshe Shelley]]'s "[[Ozymandias]]" reflects his inaccurate grasp of human history and has led to flawed conclusions. David proceeds to kill Walter.

David attacks Daniels, planning to experiment on her. Having repaired himself, Walter surprises David and defends Daniels. Team member Dan Lope is attacked by a facehugger. Cole manages to cut it off but is killed by Oram's praetomorph. ''Covenant'' pilot Tennessee uses the cargo lift to rescue Daniels, Lope, and a trailing Walter. When the praetomorph leaps aboard, Daniels confronts it and uses a loading arm to crush it.

Back on the ''Covenant'', a praetomorph hatches from Lope's chest. Daniels and Tennessee lure it into the [[terraforming]] bay and eject it into space.

The ship resumes its journey to Origae-6. As Walter places Daniels into stasis, she realizes he is actually David. Before she can act, the stasis pod renders her unconscious. David sends a transmission claiming that the crew, except Daniels and Tennessee, were killed in the neutrino burst. He regurgitates two facehugger embryos and surveys the slumbering colonists, planning to use them in his experiments.

== Production ==
=== Development ===
[[File:NASA Journey to Mars and “The Martian” (201508180030HQ).jpg|thumb|200px|Director Scott in 2015]]
''Alien: Covenant'' is the second film in the [[Alien (franchise)#Prequel series|''Alien'' prequel series]], and the sixth installment in the [[Alien (franchise)|''Alien'' franchise]]. It is the third ''Alien'' film to be directed by [[Ridley Scott]]. In 2012, prior to the release of ''Prometheus'', the first prequel (the fifth ''Alien'' film overall), director Ridley Scott began hinting at the prospect of a sequel, as ''Prometheus'' had left many questions unanswered.<ref name="COL-20170522">{{cite web |last=Chitwood |first=Adam |title='Alien: Covenant': The Original Idea for the 'Prometheus' Sequel Was Very Different |url=https://collider.com/alien-covenant-original-story-prometheus-2/ |date=22 May 2017 |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=22 May 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826125445/https://collider.com/alien-covenant-original-story-prometheus-2/|archive-date=August 26, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Sequel2">{{cite web|first=Dave |last=Trumbore |title=WonderCon 2012: Prometheus Panel Recap Featuring Sir Ridley Scott and Damon Lindelof |url=https://collider.com/prometheus-wondercon/ |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |date=March 17, 2012 |access-date=March 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120621055323/http://collider.com/prometheus-wondercon/152633 |archive-date=June 21, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Sequel1">{{cite news|last=Kit |first=Borys |url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/wondercon-2012-ridley-scott-prometheus-extended-trailer-301378 |title=WonderCon 2012: Ridley Scott Talks 'Prometheus' As Extended Trailer Debuts (Video) |publisher=[[Prometheus Global Media]] |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=March 17, 2011 |access-date=March 18, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120501211131/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/wondercon-2012-ridley-scott-prometheus-extended-trailer-301378 |archive-date=May 1, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> He said a sequel would follow Shaw, the [[protagonist]] of ''Prometheus'', to her next destination, "because if it is paradise, paradise cannot be what you think it is. Paradise has a connotation of being extremely sinister and ominous." ''Prometheus'' co-writer [[Damon Lindelof]] cast doubt on his own participation, saying, "if [Scott] wants me to be involved in something, that would be hard to say no to. At the same time, I do feel like the movie might benefit from a fresh voice or a fresh take or a fresh thought."<ref name="Sequel6">{{cite web |first=Adam |last=Chitwood |title=Prometheus Sequel Recap: What We Know About the Possible Follow-Up So Far |url=https://collider.com/prometheus-2-sequel/ |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|date=June 11, 2012 |access-date=June 12, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615115140/https://collider.com/prometheus-2-sequel/172444/|archive-date=June 15, 2012|url-status=live }}{{better source needed|date=March 2025|reason=Per [[WP:RSP/VALNET]], we try to find alternatives to ValNet published sources with some exceptions}}</ref> In June, Scott said an additional film would be required to bridge the >100-year gap between the ''Prometheus'' sequel and ''Alien''.<ref name="Sequel7">{{cite news|url=http://downloads.bbc.co.uk/podcasts/fivelive/kermode/kermode_20120601-1008a.mp3 |title=Sir Ridley Scott, 1 June 12 |author=Scott, Ridley |work=[[BBC Online]] |quote=Yeah, it's not the same planet at all. No. If there was a sequel to this, which there might be if the film is successful, there'll be two more of these before you even get to ''Alien 1''. |date=June 1, 2012 |access-date=June 17, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110183808/http://downloads.bbc.co.uk/podcasts/fivelive/kermode/kermode_20120601-1008a.mp3 |archive-date=November 10, 2013 }}</ref>

By August 1, 2012, [[20th Century Fox]] was pursuing a sequel with Scott, Noomi Rapace and [[Michael Fassbender]] involved, and talking to new writers in case Lindelof did not return.<ref name="Sequel8">{{cite news| last=McClintock |first=Pamela |url=https://hollywoodreporter.com/news/summer-movie-franchise-avengers-snow-white-magic-mike-356583 |title=Summer's Studio Smackdown: From 'Men in Black 3' to 'Prometheus,' Which Franchises Will Get Another Chapter |publisher=Prometheus Global Media |work=The Hollywood Reporter |date=August 1, 2012 |access-date=August 1, 2012}}</ref> In December 2012, Lindelof ultimately chose not to work on the project.<ref name="SequelDec2012">{{cite web|first= Steve |last=Weintraub |title=Exclusive: Damon Lindelof Is Not Writing the Prometheus Sequel; Explains Why |url=https://collider.com/prometheus-sequel-damon-lindelof/ |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|date=December 19, 2012 |access-date=December 20, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130430000310/http://collider.com/prometheus-sequel-damon-lindelof/219084|archive-date=April 30, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> Early on, Scott stated the film would feature no [[Alien (creature in Alien franchise)|xenomorphs]] as he wanted to phase the xenomorph out to focus on David 8, whose [[Artificial intelligence|A.I.]] was the new alien lifeform.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Falk |first1=Ben |title=Ridley Scott Updates Us On Prometheus 2 And Blade Runner Sequel |url=https://uk.yahoo.com/movies/ridley-scott-updates-us-on-prometheus-2-and-blade-98235330841.html |access-date=September 26, 2014 |work=[[Yahoo! Movies]] |date=September 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929041604/https://uk.movies.yahoo.com/ridley-scott-updates-us-on-prometheus-2-and-blade-98235330841.html|archive-date=September 29, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Cotter |first1=Padraig |title=The Alien Prequels Are Better Than The Predator|url=https://screenrant.com/alien-prequels-better-predator-movies/ |access-date=January 16, 2022 |work=[[Screen Rant]]|date=11 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220116041942/https://screenrant.com/alien-prequels-better-predator-movies/|archive-date=January 16, 2022|url-status=live }}</ref> He later made statements confirming the xenomorph's presence in the film, mainly due to feedback to ''Prometheus''.<ref name="TheWrap">{{cite news |last1=McKittrick |first1=Christopher |title="We wanted to create a really frightening movie!" John Logan on Alien: Covenant |url=https://creativescreenwriting.com/alien-covenant/ |access-date=May 22, 2017 |work=[[TheWrap]] |date=May 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220618033754/https://www.creativescreenwriting.com/alien-covenant/|archive-date=June 18, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/alien-covenant-ridley-scott-admits-got-prometheus-wrong-teases-two-alien-sequels-exclusive-144721534.html|title=Ridley Scott admits he got Prometheus 'wrong', teases two Alien: Covenant sequels (exclusive)|first=Tom|last=Butler|date=May 10, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|publisher=[[Yahoo! Movies]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929034826/https://uk.news.yahoo.com/alien-covenant-ridley-scott-admits-got-prometheus-wrong-teases-two-alien-sequels-exclusive-144721534.html|archive-date=September 29, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

On September 24, 2015, Scott disclosed the film's title as ''Alien: Paradise Lost''.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Han |first1=Angie |title=Ridley Scott Announces New 'Prometheus 2' Title |url=http://www.slashfilm.com/prometheus-2-title/|website=/Film |access-date=October 15, 2022|date=September 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922195513/https://www.slashfilm.com/540139/prometheus-2-title/|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> In November 2015, he revealed the new title was ''Alien: Covenant'', and that filming would begin in February 2016 in Australia.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Perez |first1=Rodrigo |title=Ridley Scott Says 'Alien: Paradise Lost' Will Now Be Called 'Alien: Covenant' |url=http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/ridley-scott-says-alien-paradise-lost-will-be-now-called-alien-covenant-20151113 |access-date=November 15, 2015 |work=[[IndieWire]] |date=November 13, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151115130638/http://blogs.indiewire.com/theplaylist/ridley-scott-says-alien-paradise-lost-will-be-now-called-alien-covenant-20151113|archive-date=November 15, 2015|url-status=live}}</ref> An official logo, synopsis and release date were released on November 16, 2015.<ref name="collidersynopsis">{{cite news |last1=Chitwood |first1=Adam |title='Prometheus' Sequel Gets Release Date and Synopsis, But Where's Noomi Rapace? |url=https://collider.com/prometheus-2-release-date-synopsis-noomi-rapace/ |access-date=November 16, 2015 |work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|date=November 16, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922195521/https://collider.com/prometheus-2-release-date-synopsis-noomi-rapace/|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>{{better source needed|date=March 2025|reason=Per [[WP:RSP/VALNET]], we try to find alternatives to ValNet published sources with some exceptions}} In an interview about the development of the David character since ''Prometheus'', Scott described the dark turn David would take in ''Covenant:'' "He hates them. He has no respect for Engineers and no respect for human beings."<ref>{{cite web |title=Ridley Scott explains why David bombed the Engineers! |website=Alien: Covenant & Sequel Movie News |url=http://www.alien-covenant.com/news/ridley-scott-explains-why-david-bombed-engineers |date=May 24, 2017|access-date=October 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803215235/https://www.alien-covenant.com/news/ridley-scott-explains-why-david-bombed-engineers|archive-date=August 3, 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Writing ===
[[File:John Logan headshot color 2009.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|After the early participation of several screenwriters, John Logan wrote the final script for the film.]]
The initial screenplay was written by ''[[Transcendence (2014 film)|Transcendence]]'' screenwriter Jack Paglen in June 2013.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Kroll|first=Justin|url=https://variety.com/2013/film/news/transcendence-scribe-to-pen-prometheus-sequel-1200478483/|title=''Prometheus 2'' Moving Forward At Fox|date=June 17, 2013|magazine=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|access-date=October 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922145133/https://variety.com/2013/film/news/transcendence-scribe-to-pen-prometheus-sequel-1200478483/|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> In March 2014, [[Michael Green (writer)|Michael Green]] was hired to rewrite Paglen's script.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sneider|first=Jeff|url=https://www.thewrap.com/prometheus-2-lands-green-lantern-writer-may-feature-multiple-michael-fassbenders-exclusive/|title=''Prometheus 2'' Lands ''Green Lantern'' Writer Michael Green|date=March 24, 2014|website=[[TheWrap]]|access-date=October 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922153312/https://www.thewrap.com/prometheus-2-lands-green-lantern-writer-may-feature-multiple-michael-fassbenders-exclusive/|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Dante Harper later wrote a new script, but an extensive rewrite was performed by screenwriter [[John Logan (writer)|John Logan]]. Logan had previously worked with Scott on ''[[Gladiator (2000 film)|Gladiator]]''.<ref name="TheWrap"/>

For Logan, the main concept was to adopt a dual plot line for the film that would combine the horror elements of ''Alien'' with the philosophical elements of ''Prometheus''. He said, "With ''Alien: Covenant'', I just really wanted to write something that had the feel of the original ''Alien'', because seeing that movie was one of the great events of my youth. It was so overpowering in terms of what it communicated to me and its implications, that when I started talking to Ridley about what became ''Alien: Covenant'', I said, 'You know, that was a hell of a scary movie.' I wanted to write a horror movie because the [[Grand Guignol]] elements of ''Alien'' are so profound. We tried to recapture that with ''Alien: Covenant'', while also trying to pay homage to the deeper implications of ''Prometheus''. In terms of tone, pace, and how we chose to play this particular symphony, we wanted to create a really frightening movie."<ref name="TheWrap" />

=== Design and visual effects ===
[[Adam Savage]] went on a tour of several of the props and stage sets used in the filming which included an alien spaceship which had first appeared in ''Prometheus''. This set had to be recreated for ''Alien: Covenant'' as the set used in ''Prometheus'' had been destroyed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mythbusters' Adam Savage Toured The Set Of Alien: Covenant, And It's Wonderful |first=Conner |last=Schwerdtfeger
|url=https://cinemablend.com/news/1653989/mythbusters-adam-savage-toured-the-set-of-alien-covenant-and-its-wonderful |work=CinemaBlend |date=May 2, 2017|access-date=September 28, 2022}}</ref> In an article for ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'', Patrick Shanley interviewed the art director for the film, Damien Drew, and creature design supervisor [[Conor O'Sullivan (make-up artist)|Conor O'Sullivan]] regarding the involvement of the [[San Diego Zoo]] and its representative Rick Schwartz as a consultant for the design of the realistic effects of the creatures and Xenomorphs appearing throughout the film as Scott wanted a more 'organic' feeling to the creatures as opposed to the 'biomechanical' inspiration of [[H.R. Giger]] which had inspired the creature designs in the original films.<ref name="organic"/> Scott provided anatomical studies and references from [[La Specola]], a natural history museum in [[Florence]], to O'Sullivan as inspiration.<ref name="organic">{{cite news |first=Patrick |last=Shanley |date=May 18, 2017 |access-date=September 28, 2022|title='Alien: Covenant': How the Xenomorph Continues to Horrify Audiences Decades Later |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |url=https://hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/alien-covenant-alien-types-xenomorph-continues-horrify-audiences-1004459}}</ref>

The [[visual effects]] (VFX) supervisor Charles Henley summarized the several vendors that were used to support production of the visual special effects seen in the film when the selection process was discussed, stating, "Both history and need guided the decisions on which vendors we used. Ridley had worked with MPC on many previous projects, in particular ''Prometheus'' for which I was [[Moving Picture Company]]'s (MPC) VFX supervisor as well as ''[[The Martian (film)|The Martian]]''. There had a been a lot of great digital double and creature work done at MPC on recent projects so there was confidence they should be the lead facility. [[Framestore]] had recently collaborated with Ridley on space for ''The Martian'', similarly Animal Logic now had the original crew who did the holograms for ''Prometheus''. Also as we were shooting in Australia there was good reason and incentives to use Australian-based companies and so Luma and Rising Sun came on board."<ref>{{cite web |title=ALIEN – COVENANT: Charley Henley – Production VFX Supervisor – MPC|website=The Art of VFX |first=Vincent |last=Frei |date=June 2, 2017 |access-date=September 28, 2022|url=http://www.artofvfx.com/alien-covenant-charley-henley-production-vfx-supervisor-mpc/}}</ref>

=== Filming ===
[[File:Milford sound Nouvelle Zélande 03 mars 2005.jpg|thumb|upright=1.1|[[Milford Sound]] was used for [[principal photography]].]]

=== Post-production ===
[[Pietro Scalia]], the editor of the film, spoke of the structural difficulty of integrating the two story lines in the final editing of the film and how the need to keep momentum was important. He did this by not repeatedly jumping between scenes which he said made parts of the film "belaboured and tedious", as well as combining certain scenes and eliminating others. Another issue highlighted was the reveal of David as;

 {{Cquote|"Once the Covenant Story merges with the Prometheus storyline finding the proper structural order of the scenes proved to be difficult because of the distinctive dynamics of the two story lines in addition to the separation of the two locations of the action. In one sense the action, the tension and unfolding drama going from one group to the other had to be balanced and spaced properly as not to loose{{Sic|nolink=y}} the connective tissue of the film."<ref>{{cite web |title=ART OF THE CUT on Ridley Scott's Alien: Covenant, with two time Oscar-winning editor, Pietro Scalia, ACE |first=Steve |last=Hullfish |date=June 26, 2017 |accessdate=December 6, 2023|work=ProVideo Coalition 
 |url=https://www.provideocoalition.com/AOTC-alien-covenant-SCALIA}}</ref>}}

Scott said the first cut of the film was two hours and 23 minutes long, which was eventually edited down to 2 hours and 3 minutes for the released version. Scott used test screenings to decide what to cut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/alien-covenant-ridley-scott-michael-fassbender-interview/#images|title=Ridley Scott and Michael Fassbender on How They Pulled Off That David/Walter Scene in 'Alien: Covenant'|first=Steve|last=Weintraub|date=May 26, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|publisher=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929042938/https://collider.com/alien-covenant-ridley-scott-michael-fassbender-interview/|archive-date=September 29, 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="digitalspy 2017-05-31"/>

== Music ==
{{Main|Alien: Covenant (soundtrack)}}
The [[film score|musical score]] for ''Alien: Covenant'' was written by Australian musician and composer [[Jed Kurzel]]. Initially, [[Harry Gregson-Williams]] was selected as the film's composer.<ref name="tapped">{{cite web |url=https://empireonline.com/people/michael-fassbender/alien-covenant-benjamin-rigby-ridley-scott/ |title=Alien: Covenant – Benjamin Rigby joins the cast|first=Owen|last=Williams |date=March 15, 2016 |work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |access-date=August 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220407135454/https://www.empireonline.com/movies/news/alien-covenant-benjamin-rigby-ridley-scott/|archive-date=April 7, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> When the first trailer was released in late 2016, Kurzel was revealed as the replacement for Gregson-Williams.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://filmmusicreporter.com/2016/12/25/jed-kurzel-to-score-ridley-scotts-alien-covenant/ |title=Jed Kurzel to Score Ridley Scott's 'Alien: Covenant'|date=December 25, 2016}}</ref> Themes from [[Jerry Goldsmith]]'s original score for ''Alien'' were incorporated, as well as themes from [[Marc Streitenfeld]]'s and Harry Gregson-Williams' score for ''Prometheus''.<ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDlcyFh_-rs&t=2777s| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190323195312/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oDlcyFh_-rs&gl=US&hl=en| archive-date=March 23, 2019|title=Jed Kurzel's Full Score For Ridley Scott's Sci-fi Horror Film "Alien: Covenant" |format= video |via= [[YouTube]] }}</ref> A version of "[[Nature Boy]]" sung by Norwegian singer and songwriter [[Aurora (singer)|Aurora]] was used in the first trailer, while another song, "[[All My Demons Greeting Me as a Friend|Under the Water]]", was used in a short promotional film featuring the character Daniels (Katherine Waterston) battling a xenomorph.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d8LJSuO4aXA| archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211030/d8LJSuO4aXA| archive-date=October 30, 2021|title=Alien: Covenant – She Won't Go Quietly | date=May 5, 2017|format=video |via= [[YouTube]] }}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a670539/alien-covenant-everything-you-need-to-know-about-prometheus-2-including-release-date-cast-and-spoilers/|title=Alien: Covenant release date, cast, spoilers and everything you need to know about Prometheus 2|first1=Rosie|last1=Fletcher|first2=Hugo|last2=Armitage|date=May 8, 2017 |work=[[Digital Spy]]|access-date=October 19, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104220017/https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a670539/alien-covenant-everything-you-need-to-know-about-prometheus-2-including-release-date-cast-and-spoilers/|archive-date=November 4, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Melanie De Biasio]]'s track "I Feel You – [[Eels (band)|Eels]] Remix" was used as the soundtrack for the in-universe short film ''Meet Walter'', starring Michael Fassbender, that was created to promote the film.<ref>{{cite web|author= ((Software A7)) |url= http://www.wallonia.be/en/news/melanie-de-biasio-lends-her-voice-alien-covenant |title= Melanie De Biasio lends her voice in Alien – Covenant |publisher= Wallonia|access-date=April 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220216082525/http://www.wallonia.be/en/news/melanie-de-biasio-lends-her-voice-alien-covenant|archive-date=February 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

Additional song credits include "Theme from ''[[Alien (film)|Alien]]''" composed by Jerry Goldsmith, "[[Das Rheingold]], Scene 4: Entrance of the Gods into Valhalla" composed by [[Richard Wagner]] (in the soundtrack, incorrectly called by David as 'Das Rheingold, Act II' - the opera has only one act)<ref name="newyorker">{{cite magazine|url=http://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/alien-covenant-bursts-with-pomposity|title="Alien: Covenant" Bursts with Pomposity|date=May 24, 2017|magazine=[[The New Yorker]]|publisher=[[Advance Publications]]|last1=Brody|first1=Richard|access-date=May 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922104543/https://www.newyorker.com/culture/richard-brody/alien-covenant-bursts-with-pomposity|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> "[[Take Me Home, Country Roads]]" by [[John Denver]], "[[The Man Who Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo (song)|The Man Who Broke the Bank at Monte Carlo]]" by [[Fred Gilbert (songwriter)|Fred Gilbert]], "Ancient Flute", "Life" and "We Were Right" composed by Harry Gregson-Williams, and "[[Let Me Down Easy (Paolo Nutini song)|Let Me Down Easy]]" by [[Paolo Nutini]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.soundtrack.net/movie/alien-covenant/|title=Alien: Covenant – Song Credits|website=[[Soundtrack.Net]]|access-date=May 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726231828/https://www.soundtrack.net/movie/alien-covenant/|archive-date=July 26, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Release ==
In the run up to release, 20th Century Fox released a number of short prologue films as part of the marketing for ''Alien: Covenant''. The first, called ''Prologue: Last Supper'', was directed by Ridley Scott's son [[Luke Scott (director)|Luke Scott]] and features the crew of the Covenant having a last meal before they enter cryosleep.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/alien-covenant-prologue/|title='Alien: Covenant': 5-Minute Prologue Reveals the Last Supper of the Covenant Crew|first=Adam|last=Chitwood|date=February 22, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|publisher=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928212344/https://collider.com/alien-covenant-prologue/|archive-date=September 28, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>{{better source Scott, reveals what happened to Elizabeth Shaw (Noomi Rapace) and the android David (Michael Fassbender) following the ending of ''Prometheus''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://collider.com/alien-covenant-shaw-david-explained/|title='Alien: Covenant' Prologue Reveals the Fate of Shaw and David Post-'Prometheus'|first=Dave|last=Trumbore|date=April 26, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|publisher=[[Collider (website)|Collider]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928212339/https://collider.com/alien-covenant-shaw-david-explained/|archive-date=September 28, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>{{better web|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20170310005368/en/Twentieth-Century-Fox-and-AMD-Partner-on-%E2%80%9CAlien-Covenant%E2%80%9D-and-Launch-%E2%80%9CMeet-Walter%E2%80%9D-Campaign|title=Twentieth ''Alien: Covenant'' premiered on May 4, 2017, at the [[Odeon Leicester Square]] in London.<ref name="firstshowing">{{Cite news|url=http://www.firstshowing.net/2017/run-pray-hide-three-new-tv-spots-for-ridley-scotts-alien-covenant/ |title=Run, Pray, Hide: Three New TV Spots for Ridley Scott's 'Alien: Covenant' |first=Alex|last=Billington|publisher=FirstShowing.net |access-date=April 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016224058/https://www.firstshowing.net/2017/run-pray-hide-three-new-tv-spots-for-ridley-scotts-alien-covenant/|archive-date=October 16, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The film was released on May 19 in the United States.<ref name="launchingfilms">{{Cite web|url=http://www.launchingfilms.com/release-schedule?filmSearch=Alien:+Covenant|title=Past, present and future releases to Past, Present and Future Releases {{!}} UK Recent and Upcoming Movie|website=launchingfilms.com|access-date=March 30, 2017|archive-date=August 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190815013015/https://www.launchingfilms.com/release-schedule?filmSearch=Alien:%2BCovenant|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="fandango">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fandango.com/alien:covenant_188982/movieoverview|title=Alien: Covenant (2017) {{!}} Fandango|work=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]] |access-date=May 10, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428104044/https://www.fandango.com/alien-covenant-188982/movie-overview|archive-date=April 28, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="firstshowing" /> It was originally set to be released on October 6, 2017, before being moved up to August 4, and then again to its final date.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Perry |first1=Spencer |title=Alien: Covenant Gets a Title Treatment, Release Date and Synopsis! The version of the film released in China on June 16, 2017, was six minutes shorter than the version released elsewhere due to [[film censorship in China|censorship]] with most of the scenes involving the aliens<ref>{{cite web|last1=Liu|first1=Charles|title=China Censored Version of 'Alien: Covenant' Has Next to No Alien in It|url=https://www.thebeijinger.com/blog/2017/06/08/china-censored-version-alien-covenant-has-next-no-alien-it|access-date=June 11, 2017|date=June 8, 2017|publisher=[[The Beijinger]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928205029/https://www.thebeijinger.com/blog/2017/06/08/china-censored-version-alien-covenant-has-next-no-alien-it|archive-date=September 28, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> and a scene where the two characters played by Michael Fassbender kiss having been cut.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/chinese-censors-cut-michael-fassbenders-gay-kiss-alien-covenant-1014488/|title=Chinese Censors Cut Michael Fassbender's Gay Kiss From 'Alien: Covenant'|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|first=Partick|last=Brzeski|date=June 18, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/movies/a831114/michael-fassbender-gay-kiss-alien-covenant-cut-by-censors-china/|title=Michael Fassbender's gay kiss in Alien: Covenant was cut by censors in China alongside five further minutes of content|work=[[Digital Spy]]|first=Louise|last=McCreesh|date=June 19, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2022}}</ref>

===Home media===
The film was released in Japan on September 15, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/05/aamir-khan-dangal-alien-covenant-guardians-of-the-glaxy-vol-2-beauty-beast-get-out-china-international-box-office-1202099242/|title='Alien: Covenant' Adds $30M In 2nd Frame; 'Dangal' Pins $100M+ In China; 'Guardians 2' At $733M WW – International Box Office|first=Nancy|last=Tartaglione|date=May 21, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|publisher=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929105036/https://deadline.com/2017/05/aamir-khan-dangal-alien-covenant-guardians-of-the-glaxy-vol-2-beauty-beast-get-out-china-international-box-office-1202099242/|archive-date=September 29, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The [[Blu-ray]], [[DVD]], and [[4K resolution#CEA Ultra HD|4K Ultra HD]] releases of the film came out on August 15, 2017. The home release includes an audio commentary by the director and 22 minutes of deleted scenes and unused footage from the first cut of the film.<ref name="Perry-2017">{{cite web|url=https://comingsoon.net/dvd/news/864883-alien-covenant-blu-ray-dvd-and-digital-release-set-for-august#/slide/1|title=Alien: Covenant Blu-ray, DVD, and Digital Release Set for August|first=Spencer|last=Perry|date=July 6, 2017|website=[[ComingSoon.net]]|archive-date=July 9, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170709093533/http://www.comingsoon.net/dvd/news/864883-alien-covenant-blu-ray-dvd-and-digital-release-set-for-august#/slide/1|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Adaptations==
=== Novelization ===
The theatrical release of the film was accompanied by the release of a [[novelization]] by [[Alan Dean Foster]], who also authored the novelization of the original ''Alien'' film.<ref>{{cite book|first=Alan Dean |last=Foster |authorlink=Alan Dean Foster|date=2017|title=Alien: Covenant|publisher=[[Titan Books]]|location=London, England|ISBN=1785654780}}</ref> A companion volume about the film's art and stage design was released at the same time, written by Simon Ward and titled ''The Art and Making of Alien: Covenant''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Ward|first=Simon|date=2017|title=The Art and Making of Alien: Covenant|publisher=[[Titan Books]]|location=London, England|ISBN=1785653814}}</ref>

A second ''Covenant'' novel by Foster was initially billed as a sequel to the film, ''Alien: Covenant 2'', before being revealed to be a direct prequel to ''Covenant'' under the title ''[[Alien: Covenant – Origins]]''.<ref>''[[Alien: Covenant – Origins|Alien: Covenant 2]]''. 304 pages; Publisher: Titan Books (September 26, 2017); Language: English; {{ISBN|1785654764}}.</ref> ''Titan Books'', as publisher of the book, released a plot summary in advance of its release on September 26, 2017:{{blockquote|As the colony ship ''Covenant'' prepares for launch, and the final members of the crew are chosen, a series of violent events reveals a conspiracy to sabotage the launch. Yet the perpetrators remain hidden behind a veil of secrecy. The threat reaches all the way up to Hideo Yutani—the head of the newly merged Weyland-Yutani Corporation—when his daughter is kidnapped. Is the conspiracy the product of corporate espionage, or is it something even more sinister? While Captain Jacob Branson{{efn|The novel's first edition and audiobook mistakenly refer to Jacob Branson as Jacob Brandon throughout.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/what-the-alien-covenant-prequel-novel-reveals-about-the-film/|title=What the Alien: Covenant Prequel Novel Reveals About the Film|first=Padraig|last=Cotter|date=November 17, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|work=[[Den of Geek]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929171550/https://www.denofgeek.com/movies/what-the-alien-covenant-prequel-novel-reveals-about-the-film/|archive-date=September 29, 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref>}} and his wife Daniels prepare the ship, Security chief Dan Lopé signs a key member of his team, and together they seek to stop the technologically advanced saboteurs before anyone else is killed, and the ship itself is destroyed in orbit.<ref>{{cite web |title=Here's the Plot for Prequel Novel 'Alien: Covenant – Origins' |first=John |last=Squires |date=June 8, 2017 |url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/news/3441058/heres-plot-prequel-novel-alien-covenant-origins/ |work=[[Bloody Disgusting]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929032544/https://bloody-disgusting.com/news/3441058/heres-plot-prequel-novel-alien-covenant-origins/|archive-date=September 29, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>}}

=== Virtual reality ===
On April 26, 2017, 20th Century Fox released ''Alien: Covenant In Utero'', a [[virtual reality]] interactive demo teaser for ''Alien: Covenant'' for the [[Oculus Rift]] and the [[Samsung Gear VR]]. The experience was produced by Ridley Scott Associates, FoxNext VR, Moving Picture Company, Mach1, [[Radeon|AMD Radeon]], and [[Alienware|Dell Alienware]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2017/04/25/with-the-new-alien-covenant-vr-experience-be-the-alien-you-want-to-see-in-the-theaters/|title=Be the alien you want to see in the theatres with the new Alien: Covenant VR experience|first=Jonathan|last=Shieber|date=April 25, 2017|access-date=September 6, 2022| publisher=[[TechCrunch]]|website=techcrunch.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427055943/https://techcrunch.com/2017/04/25/with-the-new-alien-covenant-vr-experience-be-the-alien-you-want-to-see-in-the-theaters/|archive-date=April 27, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://alien.technicolor.com/|title=A VR Experience is Born|date=2 May 2017|access-date=September 6, 2022|work=technicolor.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112024018/https://www.technicolor.com/case-studies/alien-covenant-in-utero|archive-date=November 12, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> The trailer is a first-person experience in which the viewer plays the role of a neomorph. The experience was executive produced by Scott and directed by [[David Karlak]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-in-utero-vr-experience-regal-cinemas-ridley-scott-1202084044/|title='Alien: Covenant In Utero' VR Experience Invades Regal Cinemas & Provides Terrifying Run-In With Baby Chomper|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|date=May 4, 2017|access-date=September 27, 2022|publisher=[[Deadline Hollywood|Deadline]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930050701/https://deadline.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-in-utero-vr-experience-regal-cinemas-ridley-scott-1202084044/|archive-date=September 30, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Reception ==
=== Box office ===
''Alien: Covenant'' grossed a worldwide total of $242.4 million, including $74.3 million in the United States and Canada and $168.1 million in other countries, against a production budget of $97–111 million.<ref name="BOM" /><ref name="NUM" /><ref name="sleeper1"/><ref name="sleeper2"/> Although the film performed better overseas than domestically, it was still considered a disappointment at the box office compared to ''[[Prometheus (2012 film)|Prometheus]]'' which had grossed a worldwide total of $403.4 million.<ref name="starwars">{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2017/film/news/alien-covenant-box-office-analysis-ridley-scott-1202439346/|title=Sorry, Ridley Scott: The 'Alien' Franchise Is No 'Star Wars'|first=Seth|last=Kelley|date=May 21, 2017 |access-date=October 5, 2022|publisher=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007230009/https://variety.com/2017/film/news/alien-covenant-box-office-analysis-ridley-scott-1202439346/|archive-date=October 7, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="BOMProm">{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/title/tt1446714/ |title=Prometheus |work=Box Office Mojo |date=June 2, 2012 |access-date=September 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120619145013/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=prometheus.htm |archive-date=June 19, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Fox released the film in several countries before the United States.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/la-et-mn-alien-covenant-review-20170517-story.html|title=Ridley Scott's 'Alien: Covenant' is a sleek, suspenseful return to form|last=Chang|first=Justin|date=May 17, 2017|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|access-date=May 19, 2017|issn=0458-3035|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210707160933/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/la-et-mn-alien-covenant-review-20170517-story.html|archive-date=July 7, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.tracking-board.com/alien-covenant-film-review-ridley-scott-returns-to-form-with-chest-bursting-thrills/|title="Alien: Covenant" Film Review: Ridley Scott Returns to Form With Chest-Bursting Thrills|date=7 May 2017|publisher=The Tracking Board|access-date=19 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226202731/https://www.tracking-board.com/alien-covenant-film-review-ridley-scott-returns-to-form-with-chest-bursting-thrills/|archive-date=December 26, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> It was released in 34 markets, where it debuted to $40.1 million, opening at number one in 19 of them. === Critical response ===
[[File:Michael Fassbender by Gage Skidmore 2015.jpg|thumb|upright=0.85|Fassbender's portrayal of two similar androids with different programming, [[David 8|David]] and [[Walter One|Walter]], was highly praised by reviewers.]]
''Alien: Covenant'' received generally positive reviews from critics.<ref>Multiple sources:
* {{cite web | last=Shepherd | first=Jack | title=Here's what the critics are saying about Alien: Covenant | work=[[The Independent]] | date=May 7, 2017 | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/alien-covenant-reviews-roundup-prometheus-aliens-critics-a7722226.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211226202741/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/alien-covenant-reviews-roundup-prometheus-aliens-critics-a7722226.html |archive-date=December 26, 2021 |url-access=limited |url-status=live | access-date=March 23, 2021}}
* {{cite web |url=https://www.indiewire.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-critical-roundup-michael-fassbender-1201813409/ |title='Alien: Covenant' Critical Roundup: Michael Fassbender Is Singled Out for Praise in Early Reviews of Ridley Scott's Latest |last=Nordine |first=Michael |date=May 7, 2017 |work=[[IndieWire]]|access-date=March 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220516161757/https://www.indiewire.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-critical-roundup-michael-fassbender-1201813409/|archive-date=May 16, 2022|url-status=live}}
* {{cite web | title=Here's What the Critics Are Saying About 'Alien: Covenant' | first=Nivea |last=Serrao| website=EW.com | publisher=[[Entertainment Weekly]]| date=May 7, 2017 | url=https://ew.com/movies/2017/05/07/alien-covenant-reviews-roundup/ | access-date=March 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220528165506/https://ew.com/movies/2017/05/07/alien-covenant-reviews-roundup/|archive-date=May 28, 2022|url-status=live}}
* {{cite web | last=Rahman | first=Abid | title=Alien Covenant Review Round-Up | publisher=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=May 8, 2017 | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/heat-vision/alien-covenant-review-round-up-1001062 | access-date=March 23, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220529213547/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movies/movie-news/alien-covenant-review-round-up-1001062/|archive-date=May 29, 2022|url-status=live}}
* {{cite web | title=Alien: Covenant Review Roundup | publisher=[[GameSpot]] | url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/alien-covenant-review-roundup/1100-6449923/ | first= Eddie |last=Makuch| date=May 18, 2017| access-date=September 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220410120436/https://www.gamespot.com/articles/alien-covenant-review-roundup/1100-6449923/|archive-date=April 10, 2022|url-status=live }}
* {{Cite news |url=http://www.slashfilm.com/alien-covenant-reviews/ |title=Alien Covenant Reviews Round-up | first=Ethan |last=Anderton| date=May 8, 2017 |work=[[/Film]] |access-date=May 19, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220914212418/https://www.slashfilm.com/550818/alien-covenant-reviews/|archive-date=September 14, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> The film has {{a or an|{{RT data|score}}}} approval from {{RT data|count}} reviews compiled by review aggregation website [[Rotten Tomatoes]], with an average rating of {{RT data|average}}. The website's critical consensus reads, "''Alien: Covenant'' delivers another satisfying round of close-quarters deep-space terror, even if it doesn't take the saga in any new directions."<ref name="tomatoes">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/alien_covenant|title=Alien: Covenant|website=[[Rotten Tomatoes]]|publisher=[[Fandango Media|Fandango]]|access-date={{RT data|access date|df=mdy}}|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922212103/https://www.rottentomatoes.com/m/alien_covenant|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}{{RT data|edit}}</ref> On [[Metacritic]], the film has a score of 65 out of 100, based on reviews from 52 critics, indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{cite web |title= Alien: Covenant reviews |website= [[Metacritic]] |publisher=[[CBS Interactive|CBS Interactive Inc.]] |url= https://metacritic.com/movie/alien-covenant |access-date= September 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922201617/https://www.metacritic.com/movie/alien-covenant|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live }}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale, the same score earned by its predecessor.<ref name="opening" />

Writing for ''[[The Guardian]]'', [[Peter Bradshaw]] gave the film three stars out of five, stating that ''Alien: Covenant'' is "a greatest-hits compilation of the other ''Alien'' films' freaky moments. The paradox is that though you are intended to recognize these touches, you won't really be impressed unless you happen to be seeing them for the first time. For all this, the film is very capably made, with forceful, potent performances from Waterston and Fassbender."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2017/may/07/alien-covenant-review-ridley-scott-michael-fassbender-katherine-waterston-prometheus|title=Alien: Covenant review – Ridley Scott's latest space exploration feels all too familiar|first=Peter|last=Bradshaw|author-link=Peter Bradshaw|date=May 6, 2017| access-date= September 5, 2022| work=[[The Guardian]]|publisher=[[Guardian Media Group|Guardian News and Media Limited]]|location=London|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221015133741/https://www.theguardian.com/film/2017/may/07/alien-covenant-review-ridley-scott-michael-fassbender-katherine-waterston-prometheus|archive-date=October 15, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Geoffrey McNab, writing for ''[[The Independent]]'', stated that it "certainly delivers what you'd expect from an ''Aliens'' film—spectacle, body horror, strong [[Ellen Ripley|Ripley]]-like female protagonists and some astonishing special effects—but there's also a dispiriting sense that the film isn't at all sure of its own identity." He found the screenplay "very portentous" and concluded that "the crew members pitted against the monstrous creatures are trying their darndest to blast them to kingdom come, just as they would in any run-of-the-mill sci-fi B movie."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/film-reviews-round-up-alien-covenant-frantz-jawbone-the-levelling-a7727686.html |title=Film reviews round-up: Alien: Covenant, Frantz, Jawbone, The Levelling|first=Geoffrey|last=McNab|date=May 17, 2017|access-date=September 5, 2022|work=[[The Independent]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201122201125/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/film-reviews-round-alien-covenant-frantz-jawbone-levelling-a7727686.html|archive-date=November 22, 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[A. O. Scott]] of ''[[The New York Times]]'' said, "''Alien: Covenant'' is an interesting movie ... for all its interplanetary ranging, [it] commits itself above all to the canny management of expectations."<ref name="NYT-20170517">{{cite news|last=Scott|first=A. O.|author-link=A. O. Scott|title=Review: 'Alien: Covenant' Summons Terror and Stays on Brand|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/17/movies/alien-covenant-review-ridley-scott.html|date=May 17, 2017|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=May 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404180806/https://www.nytimes.com/2017/05/17/movies/alien-covenant-review-ridley-scott.html|archive-date=April 4, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Trace Thurman, from [[Bloody Disgusting]], gave the film a mediocre review, noting that although watching ''Alien: Covenant'' will make viewers appreciate ''Prometheus'' more, "this is a film that was made as a response to ''Prometheus'' critics but tries to appease fans of that film as well and it doesn't fully work." He also criticizes the overfamiliarity of the climax and insufficiently developed characters.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bloody-disgusting.com/reviews/3436633/review-alien-covenant/|title=[Review] 'Alien: Covenant' Disappoints, Despite a Stellar Production|date=May 15, 2017 |work=[[Bloody Disgusting]]|first=Trace |last=Thurman|access-date=May 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404182239/https://bloody-disgusting.com/reviews/3436633/review-alien-covenant/|archive-date=April 4, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Collider (website)|Collider]]''{{'}}s review of the film stated that Scott "finds himself stuck between two constructs—the action-horror beats of an ''Alien'' film, and the weighty, ponderous themes of a ''Prometheus'' movie—and by indulging both, he never fully satisfies either. The result is a messy film that is at turns, exquisite and infuriating."<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://collider.com/alien-covenant-review/ |title='Alien: Covenant' Review: An Exquisite, Infuriating Epic from a Sci-Fi Master |date=May 6, 2017 |first=Haleigh|last=Foutch|work=[[Collider (website)|Collider]] |access-date=December 6, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928080059/https://collider.com/alien-covenant-review/|archive-date=September 28, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

In a review for ''The Independent'' Clarisse Loughrey gave the film five stars describing it as "relentless and overwhelming, but all in the very best of ways" and as a "mightily impressive piece of cinematic engineering" which has brought together the Alien franchise. Loughrey praised Katherine Waterston for her "impressive work" as Daniels and went on to single out Fassbender for playing a "deeply frightening, scene-stealing antagonist".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/alien-covenant-review-prometheus-sequel-prequel-michael-fassbender-david-walter-a7720371.html|title=Alien: Covenant review: It's everything you could ever want from an Alien movie|first=Clarisse|last=Loughrey|date=May 7, 2017|access-date=September 5, 2022|work=[[The Independent]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221002204323/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/reviews/alien-covenant-review-prometheus-sequel-prequel-michael-fassbender-david-walter-a7720371.html|archive-date=October 2, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Sinead Brennan for [[Raidió Teilifís Éireann|RTÉ]], gave the film 7/10, but gave high praise to Fassbender who she says "steals the show; seriously, he's incredible".<ref name="RTE">{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/entertainment/movie-reviews/2017/0509/873654-alien-covenant/|title=Alien: Covenant movie review|first=Sinead|last=Brennan|date=May 13, 2017|access-date=September 5, 2022|publisher=[[Raidió Teilifís Éireann|RTÉ]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905005852/https://www.rte.ie/entertainment/movie-reviews/2017/0509/873654-alien-covenant/|archive-date=September 5, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Meanwhile, Neil Soans in a three star review for ''[[The Times of India]]'', highlighted Danny McBride's performance as the most surprising given his comedic roots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/english/movie-reviews/alien-covenant/movie-review/58628845.cms|title=Alien: Covenant Movie Review|work=[[The Times of India]]|first=Neil|last=Soans|date=May 11, 2017|access-date=October 26, 2022}}</ref>

[[Matt Zoller Seitz]] of ''[[RogerEbert.com]]'' highly praised ''Alien: Covenant'', giving it four out of four stars and stating that the film's structure, although repeatedly borrowing from other ''Alien'' films, serves a purpose not unlike the [[James Bond in film|James Bond film series]] or ''[[Star Wars]]'', "where part of the fun lies in seeing what variations the artists can bring while satisfying a rigid structure." He also emphasized that, like previous films of the series, real-world logic should not be applied to the film, and "[i]nstead you have to judge it by the standards of a [[fever dream]] or nightmare, a [[Sigmund Freud|Freudian]]-[[Carl Jung|Jungian]] narrative where the thing you fear most is what happens to you."<ref name="ebert">{{cite web|last1=Seitz|first1=Matt Zoller|title=Alien: Covenant Movie Review & Film Summary (2017)|url=https://rogerebert.com/reviews/alien-covenant-2017|website=[[RogerEbert.com]]|publisher=Ebert Digital LLC|access-date=May 15, 2017|date=May 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204143335/https://www.rogerebert.com/reviews/alien-covenant-2017|archive-date=February 4, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref> Seitz later voted for it in ''Sight & Sound'' as one of the five best films of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=The best films of 2017 – all the votes|url=https://www2.bfi.org.uk//features/best-films-2017-all-the-votes/|website=[[Sight & Sound]]|publisher=[[British Film Institute|BFI]]|access-date=January 16, 2018|date=December 14, 2017|first1=Paul|last1= McManus|first2= Rob |last2=Philp|first3= Nick |last3=Bradshaw|first4=Isabel |last4=Stevens|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220825220621/https://www2.bfi.org.uk/features/best-films-2017-all-the-votes/|archive-date=August 25, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>

In ''[[New York (magazine)|New York]]'' magazine, [[David Edelstein]] commented on David the android as representing a new generation of monster villains in the tradition of [[Victor Frankenstein|Frankenstein]], stating, "In ''[[Star Trek]]'', that man-machine nexus was...hopeful. Here, there's some doubt about David's ultimate motives, which puts ''Alien: Covenant'' squarely in the tradition of the ''[[Terminator (franchise)|Terminator]]'' and ''[[The Matrix (franchise)|Matrix]]'' movies. And, of course, the novel ''[[Frankenstein]]'', which carried the subtitle ''The Modern Prometheus''. No less than [[Stephen Hawking]]—who survived with the aid of machines—has predicted that we have 100 years to live before evolved machines take human imperfection as [[Existential risk from artificial general intelligence|justification for destroying humanity]]".<ref>{{cite web|last1=Edelstein|first1=David|title=Review: Alien: Covenant Is an Origin Story We Might Not Have Wanted|url=http://www.vulture.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-movie-review.html|website=[[New York (magazine)#Digital|Vulture]]|date=May 16, 2017 |publisher=[[New York (magazine)|New York Media LLC]]|access-date=May 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127194257/https://www.vulture.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-movie-review.html|archive-date=November 27, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kevin Lincoln, writing for ''[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]]'', gave a strong endorsement of the depiction of David as an arch-villain in the film stating, "...{{nbsp}}one franchise is showing it's still possible for a modern blockbuster to have a great villain. In ''Alien: Covenant'', David—the android played by Michael Fassbender, first introduced in ''Prometheus''—comes into his own as a fleshed-out, dynamic, and genuinely striking antagonist, one who isn't just an equal match for the heroes, but even becomes the central thread of the series. He's a huge part of what makes ''Alien: Covenant'' work."<ref>{{cite web |last=Lincoln |first=Kevin |title=What Other Blockbuster Villains Can Learn From David in Alien: Covenant| work=[[Vulture (website)|Vulture]] |date=May 23, 2017 |url=http://www.vulture.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-david-michael-fassbender-villain.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211202133010/https://www.vulture.com/2017/05/alien-covenant-david-michael-fassbender-villain.html|archive-date=December 2, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref>

Writing for ''[[Vox Media|Vox]]'', Alissa Wilkinson said that "''Alien: Covenant'' is too muddled to pull off its deeply ambitious Satan allegories". She emphasized the [[Paradise Lost|Miltonic]] demonic aspect of the android David: "But David is a better Satan than Satan himself ... It's as if in the ''Alien'' universe, the devil has evolved, thanks to humans creating him. David, fatally, has the ability to create—something Satan never had—and he will use that power only to destroy. He doesn't have any real need to rebel against his maker, since from the moment he became sentient, he knew he'd already won. He is indestructible, and determined to make creatures that imitate his drive for total domination."<ref>Alissa Wilkinson. {{cite web|url=https://www.vox.com/summer-movies/2017/5/17/15612540/alien-covenant-review-fassbender-satan-paradise-lost-spoilers|title=Alien: Covenant is too muddled to pull off its deeply ambitious Satan allegories|first=Alissa|last=Wilkinson|publisher=[[Vox (website)|Vox]]|date=May 17, 2017|access-date=September 5, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905111758/https://www.vox.com/summer-movies/2017/5/17/15612540/alien-covenant-review-fassbender-satan-paradise-lost-spoilers|archive-date=September 5, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref>
